source_units.text: Abstract
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The world population is aging rapidly, and increasing lifespan exacerbates the burden of age-related health issues.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: On the other hand, premature aging has begun to be a problem, with increasing numbers of younger people suffering aging-related symptoms.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Advanced aging is caused by a combination of factors: lifestyle, diet, external and internal factors, as well as oxidative stress (OS).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Although OS is the most researched aging factor, it is also the least understood.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

## 1. Introduction

Healthy aging is characterized by a gradual breakdown of physiological systems leading to a reduction in cognitive functions and brain health, but the timing and extent of this decline vary among older people. Oxidative stress (OS) is a crucial factor in the aging process that can cause direct damage to the brain’s cellular architecture, causing neurodegenerative disease.

source_units.text: Aging is linked to a loss of homeostasis, involving degradation of structural components, reduced cellular maintenance and a decrease in overall physiological function/metabolism.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: There are two major aging theories: the free radical theory, which postulates chronological accumulation of defects in gene expression and environmental damage.

source_units.text: According to the free radical theory of aging by Denham Harman, 1956 [1], alterations in normal metabolic and mitochondrial function are induced by production of free radicals, which cause damage, aging, and associated aging illnesses.

source_units.text: The second and more recent theory is the mitochondrial theory of aging by J. Miquel and colleagues in 1980 [2].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

2.1. Environmental Factors: Radiation/UV Rays and Pollution

Environmental factors, including smoking, UV radiation, heavy metal ions, ozone, allergens, drugs or toxins, pollutants, and pesticides, may all contribute to elevated ROS production in cells [17,18].

source_units.text: Ionizing radiation transforms hydroxyl radicals, superoxides, and organic radicals into organic hydroperoxides and hydrogen peroxide.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Subsequently, peroxides react with metal ions, particularly Fe and Cu through redox reactions, with further oxidative activity at the cellular level.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Several studies have demonstrated that exposure of fibroblasts to alpha particles leads to an intracellular increase in oxygen and an acceleration of peroxide formation [19,20].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Ultraviolet radiation (UVA) induces oxidative processes by stimulating riboflavin, porphyrins, and NADPH-oxidase, resulting in synthesis of 8-oxo-guanine and a drop in intracellular GSH levels, with a return to normal after exposure cessation [21].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Heavy metals are crucial to the formation of free radicals [22].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

Mechanistic Evolution of Neurodegenerative Diseases Caused by OS

Neurodegenerative disease is an irreversible condition in which neuronal function declines over time, leading to neuronal death.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: The incidence of neurodegenerative disease is increasing every year, especially in countries with aging populations.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Common neurodegenerative diseases include Alzheimer’s (AD) and Parkinson’s (PD) diseases.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondria are the primary source of ROS and are the main cause of neurodegenerative diseases (Figure 2).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required
deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Mitochondrial synthesis of ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, has the substantial disadvantage of producing unpaired electrons [45,46].

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

Major Degenerative Disorders Caused by OS

### 4.1. OS in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Despite substantial investigation, the genesis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is still not fully clear.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: ALS has been linked to various occupational and environmental variables, such as exposure to various chemicals, metals, and pesticides, electromagnetic fields (EMFs), and lifestyle choices, including smoking and excessive exercise [55,56,57,58].

source_units.text: A recognized but poorly understood pathogenic ALS feature is abnormally high free radical levels and inadequate antioxidation.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Further, because of OS’s random start and the present lack of tools to forecast its progression, it is difficult to be certain whether OS is a cause of ALS-associated neurodegeneration or a result of other underlying etiologic variables [57].

OS in Alzheimer’s Disease (AD)

The most common neurodegenerative condition, AD, is characterized by a steady decline in behavior, cognition, and functioning that profoundly affect day-to-day activities.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: AD brains have higher protein, DNA, and lipid oxidation rates, as well as redox-active metals [51].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Pathological indicators of AD include extracellular senile plaques (SP) and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles (NFT).
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Protein aggregation is sporadic, and its molecular mechanism is poorly understood.
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Several investigations have revealed that AD brains display elevated OS, which is crucial to disease development [68].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Amyloid fibril precursors are neurotoxic owing to OS generated by toxic conformer of amyloid oligomers and additional neurotoxic effects such as neuronal membrane rupture, microglia and astrocyte activation, and Ca2+ dyshomeostasis [69,70,71].

OS in Multiple Sclerosis (MS)

Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a multifactorial autoimmune disease of the central nervous system (CNS), characterized by chronic inflammation, demyelination, and axon and neuron loss.

source_units.text: Depending on the location of the demyelinating lesions, MS patients can develop almost any neurological sign or symptom, including motor, sensory, and cognitive impairment [94,95].

source_units.text: OS is heavily involved in several MS pathological hallmarks such as myelin destruction, axonal degeneration, and inflammation [96].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: In MS as in other neurodegenerative diseases OS triggers activation of autophagy and microglia as well as of the neuroimmune system.

Significance of Non-Coding RNAs in OS

OS readily damages RNA due to its single-stranded structure and high concentration close to mitochondria, where most intracellular ROS are generated [107,108].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: An overabundance of ROS can cause chemical modification or even separation of RNA bases and breakage of RNA strands [91,109].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Oxidatively damaged RNA accumulates in cells, leading to decreased protein synthesis, erroneous protein generation, and ultimately cell death [110,111].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), which do not encode proteins, make up the majority of RNAs in human cells [112,113].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: As a category of ncRNAs, regulatory ncRNAs, including long ncRNAs (lncRNAs) and small ncRNAs, which includes microRNAs (miRNAs), circular RNAs (circRNAs), and PIWI-interacting RNAs (piRNAs), are involved in regulating gene expression [114].
source_units.reason: deterministic dependency projection; expert review required

source_units.text: Compared to mRNAs, these regulatory ncRNAs persist relatively longer.

source_units.text: Hence, oxidative damage can cause prolonged effects.
